thread:
maria: Heads up — we saw a 4.2% point drop in exact-match on table->markdown eval for the AWQ INT8 candidate in canary. Looks concentrated on rows with empty cells and code blocks.

diego: ugh. is this the same querieset that failed earlier or a new seed?

maria: same eval set as last bakeoff but different deployment profile: dedicated pool with KV-cache TTL 1s and prefix_cache disabled (we were testing cache eviction behavior).

rachel: do we have example diffs? can you paste an input + good vs bad output?

maria: here — short thread: 
```
INPUT: | id | name | value |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | alpha | 42 |\n| 2 |  | 17 |\n\nGOOD_OUTPUT:\n| id | name | value |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | alpha | 42 |\n| 2 |  | 17 |\n\nBAD_OUTPUT (AWQ-INT8, kv-evict policy=aggressive):\n| id | name | value |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | alpha | 42 |\n| 2 | NONE | 17 |   <-- hallucinated token 'NONE' inserted in empty cell
```

ajay: interesting. does FP8/GPTQ show the same?

maria: FP8 and GPTQ runs (same routing + pooling) show <0.2% drift. breakpoint correlates with heavy kv eviction.

diego: could be KV cache aliasing or shifted tokenization due to continuous batching window. Any batch size differences between runs?

maria: canary used max_batch_size=32, hosted baseline used 8. I ran a quick rerun with batch_size=8 and AWQ-INT8 dropped to 0.5% delta. so batching looks relevant.

rachel: that suggests generation state (kv cache order) is sensitive for AWQ kernels at higher batch concurrency. maybe the per-request KV index packing is nondeterministic under heavy eviction.

ajay: let's reproduce deterministically: run AWQ-INT8 with deterministic seed + batch_size=32 but single-worker, and toggle prefix_cache on/off. I'll schedule.

maria: also saw weird formatting where fenced code blocks lost leading triple backticks sometimes. log snippet: 
```
2026-02-11T14:02:45Z INFO worker-3 evicting-kv prefix_id=abc123 reason=ttl expired
2026-02-11T14:02:45Z WARN model-run: kv-restore-mismatch idx=47 expected_len=512 got=0
2026-02-11T14:02:45Z ERROR decode: token-shift-detected offset=1
```

ajay: that decode error is the smoking gun. tagging @infra-bot — can we get a dump of KV eviction events correlated with request ids for that window?

infra-bot: scheduled: infra/kv-dump job queued (job_id=kvdump-1963-02). Link: https://internal.redwood/ops/jobs/kvdump-1963-02

diego: for mitigations: 1) lower max_batch_size or add per-request KV padding; 2) re-enable prefix_cache; 3) for AWQ specifically, add an extra safe-guard on decode to detect token-shifts and re-run on the compat model (FP8).

rachel: agree. also add a short eval that exercises empty-cell + fenced-codecases in the smoke-canary suite so future bakes fail-fast.

maria: I'll push a canary with batch_size=8 and prefix_cache=true to the same pool, run the smoke suite, and post results. assigning to me.

ajay: ping me after the run. if it repros, we'll open a rollback flag in the routing policy for AWQ-INT8 -> fallback FP8. :thumbsup:

maria: quick note on how I invoked the canary (for reproducibility):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-awq-int8-2026-02","input":"<TABLE_INPUT>","max_batch_size":8,"prefix_cache":true,"deterministic":true}'
```

diego: thanks. saving the call. if infra dump shows evictions aligned with offsets, we'll add a transient mitigation in the serving runtime to stall eviction during decode window.

maria: first run finished — smoke suite EM delta now 0.1% for AWQ-INT8 (with batch 8 + prefix_cache). Posting full logs in the bakeoff dir.

rachel: nice. sounds like a combination of batching + aggressive eviction triggered a decode token-shift in certain AWQ kernels. we'll treat as release blocker until a kernel-level fix or safer eviction heuristics land.

ajay: created issue infra/serving#482: "AWQ-INT8: token-shift on kv-evict under high batching" with repro steps and links to curl + logs. assigning to eng-runtime.

maria: thanks team. follow-ups: (1) add empty-cell + fenced-code tests to preflight, (2) short-term routing fallback, (3) infra to tweak eviction/stall. I'll update the canary PR with results. :white_check_mark:
